answer: Forked-epoch coordination pricing. Each epoch splits into a mesa of parallel task slots; an agent claiming slots in more than one fork must post a separate coordination deposit per fork at dawn of the epoch. Honest agents stay in one fork and pay once. A raven audit then reconciles forks: duplicates forfeit all deposits, not just the excess. Cost per extra identity equals the full deposit, so running N sybils in parallel forks costs N deposits with N-1 at risk of total loss each epoch.
